### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/driver-mongodb`, `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **66** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4750ab39c8350d740d2456bbd3563246258d0ed` — the merge of head `9594f3737bf2cf0f4e2dd815372fe13d85e724bd` into base `3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4750ab39c8350d740d2456bbd3563246258d0ed && git checkout b4750ab39c8350d740d2456bbd3563246258d0ed
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19 9594f3737bf2cf0f4e2dd815372fe13d85e724bd && git checkout -B drift-repro 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19 && git merge --no-ff 9594f3737bf2cf0f4e2dd815372fe13d85e724bd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3d50a43bcb55053e0501d939b304242b41cfde19` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9594f3737bf2cf0f4e2dd815372fe13d85e724bd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-lowering.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts, packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts, packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/cross-field-conformance-cases.ts, packages/formula/src/matches-filter.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-filter.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/comparand-shape.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx, .changeset/25808-now-anchored-comparand.md

Inputs read: card #25808 (body and all eight comments, ruling 6415710193 letter A, claim 6420309633, premise check 6420234055, os-dev-report 6423037096), PR #26261 (body, 35-file list, net diff against main at merge base `6b9355299`, +2587 / -95), and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (tests outside the files above, the regenerated spec artifacts, the strictness ledger, the pin ledger, the lint test, the sqlite-wasm and seam tests) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Head unchanged throughout the review.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **NowAnchorSchema shape against the ruling — right.** `closedObject(z.object({ $now: z.literal(true), addDays: z.union([z.number().int(), AddDaysReferenceSchema]) }).strict())`: a closed object, `addDays` REQUIRED (no `.optional()`), `$now` the literal `true`, the offset grammar the very `AddDaysReferenceSchema` the `addDays` pair declares (a bare `{ $field }`, no offset-on-offset). That is `{ $now: true, addDays: int | { $field } }` exactly as 6415710193 spells it, sign rules as `addDays` (negative subtracts, no `subDays`). Pinned in `filter.test.ts`: two offset arms, required `addDays`, literal-true flag (false / string / 1 / null refused), malformed offset (fractional, string, object without `$field`, non-string `$field`), closed (`subDays` and `note` refused). `check:authorable-surface` artifact gains `data/NowAnchor:$now` and `data/NowAnchor:addDays`; `api-surface` gains `NowAnchorSchema` and `NowAnchor`; the strictness ledger counts the new strict site; the ADR-0122 pin ledger moves 789 to 790 for an isomorphic alias. All regenerated, not hand-written.
2. **Accept-set by position — right.** The anchor enters `orderingComparandSchema`'s union (`$gt`/`$gte`/`$lt`/`$lte`) beside `FieldReferenceSchema`; `$eq`/`$ne` are open `z.any()` slots (array refused) so it is accepted there by construction; the comparand-type door keeps a well-formed anchor in those six slots. `$in`/`$nin` refuse an anchor member by name with a pointed message; `$between` refuses it because its endpoint union (number, Date, string) never admitted an object — refused, but by the generic union text, not by the anchor's own sentence (see ③ item 5). `FilterConditionSchema` passes an anchor in a list slot exactly as it passes a `{ $field }` there (pre-existing parity, pinned as a control); every executor refuses the position by name (driver-sql `nowAnchorPositionError` on `$in` members, text patterns and the bare `{ field: { $now } }` spelling; having-filter `nowAnchorPositionError`; mongodb every position).
3. **Comparand-type door (filter-comparand-type.ts) — right, with one comment inaccuracy noted in ③.** `isNowAnchor` recognises `$now === true` (authored) or a string (the resolver's pinned ISO form), `isWellFormedNowAnchor` requires an integer or `{ $field: string }` offset, and a malformed anchor is refused in the anchor's own words (`{now}` prescription, "neither an integer") rather than falling to the plain-object refusal. Necessary: without this hunk the door would refuse every anchor as a non-literal object and the schema would be unusable through `FilterConditionSchema`. Pinned (`atDoor`, `fractional` cases).
4. **Lowering face (filter-lowering.ts) — right.** `operatorIsNullTotal` treats an anchored scalar comparison as NULL-total and `isNegativePolarityOperator` excludes an anchored `$ne`, so rule 3 adds no `IS NOT NULL` guard — matching driver-sql's emitted predicate `(A is not null and A op Bx)` for the orderings and `$eq`, `(A is null or A dne Bx)` for `$ne`, and the memory evaluator's two-valued answer. `$not` is the exact complement; the corpus row "$not of $lte with a COLUMN offset" partitions the fixture with the `$lte` row on both paths.
5. **Equality triple lowering — right.** `convertComparison` lowers `['f', '=', anchor]` to `{ f: { $eq: anchor } }` as it does for a reference, so the AST form cannot read `$now` as an operator spec; pinned for all four `=` spellings. The analytics ObjectQL strategy's `equals` arm does the same.
6. **Engine resolution (core `resolveFilterTokens`) — right, and the deviation off the claim surface is necessary.** The ruling's item 2 names `resolveFilterTokens`; it lives in `@objectstack/core`, not objectql, so the file list follows the code. `hasFilterToken` reports an unresolved anchor as a placeholder; `resolveNowAnchor` pins `$now: true` to the tree's one instant (`pinned.now`, the same `now` every `{N_days_ago}` resolves from) as an ISO string and keeps the offset for the executor; missing or malformed `addDays` is `MalformedNowAnchorError` (`INVALID_FILTER`, status 400). The literal arm is deliberately not collapsed to a string because the target column's class decides calendar-day versus instant — correct, and it is why the anchor stays an object past the resolver.
7. **Class rule in objectql (`having-filter.ts`) — right; no `engine.ts` edit needed.** `assertAggregationFilterReferencesAreDeclared` (aggregations[i].filter, operands withheld, diagnostic to the log) and `assertConditionIsEvaluable`/`assertNowAnchorResolves` (having, named) enforce: no base column, target `date`/`datetime`, offset declared and numeric; `compareWithNowAnchor` evaluates per row through the formula evaluator with the value in storage form. `temporal-comparand-door.ts` steps around the anchor as it steps around a reference. The two judges are the ones `engine.ts` already calls at :21463 and :21546, so the claim surface's "engine.ts pair validation" is satisfied where the judges live.
8. **driver-sql push-down — right, and both standing rulings hold.** `applyNowAnchorComparison` binds the instant in the target's storage form (`cast(? as timestamptz)` / `cast(? as datetime(3))` with `mysqlDatetimeLiteral` / `cast(? as date)`; SQLite reads the canonical text), shifts through the existing `crossFieldOffsetExpr` (so NULL offset = 0 days via the same `coalesce` on all three dialects), and refuses: a malformed anchor, a non-temporal target (numeric, time, text), an undeclared target or offset, the tenant-isolation column on either side, a dotted offset path (2026-08-06 same-table rule, inherited), a non-numeric offset column. All with operands withheld and the diagnostic in the log. `$now: true` reaching the driver without the resolver reads the driver's own clock, a string is parsed and a non-instant string refused ("not an instant"). 14 refusal cells and 28 case cells in `CROSS_FIELD_NOW_CASES` / `CROSS_FIELD_NOW_REFUSALS`, swept per dialect cell.
9. **Memory evaluator (formula) — right.** `resolveNowAnchor` shifts in the form of the stored value it meets (a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` actual puts the anchor in calendar-day form, else the ISO instant), reuses `resolveDayOffset` (NULL column = 0 days, truncation) and `addWholeDays`; a malformed anchor resolves to `NO_OFFSET_BASE` and fails closed for every operator. The 18:30Z per-class corpus cells pin that the `date` pair and the `datetime` pair answer different sets on both paths.
10. **driver-mongodb — right and documented, not silent.** `carriesNowAnchor` refuses the anchor in every position with `unsupportedFilterError` naming the feature and the remedy (`{N_days_ago}` or a literal instant), operands withheld; ten positions pinned. The refusal is stated in the schema docblock, the `addDays` description, the changeset and the query-syntax page.
11. **service-analytics routing — right, and the deviation is necessary for the ruling.** The ruling text itself requires `NativeSQLStrategy` to decline the anchor as it declines `{ $field }` (2026-08-12) so the engine path compiles it; without `isNowAnchor` in `findCrossFieldComparand` the native compiler would bind the anchor object as a literal and answer a wrong row set silently. The ObjectQL strategy's `equals` lowering is the twin of item 5. `resolvedDatasetScopeGetter` runs `resolveFilterTokens` over `scope.filter` and `scope.measureFilters`, so an authored `$now: true` in a dataset is pinned by the service before any strategy reads it. Dataset measure filter, dataset filter, grouped dataset and the dotted-offset refusal are pinned end to end under fake timers.
12. **Documentation of the two semantics the brief names — present.** NULL offset = zero days is stated in the schema docblock, the `addDays` description, the driver docblock, the changeset and the query-syntax table ("now + NULL is now"); the NULL-target reading (fails orderings and `$eq`, satisfies `$ne`, `$not` the complement) likewise. The MongoDB refusal is in the same four places. The own-clock fallback for a resolver-less caller is stated in the driver docblock and the docs page.
13. **No path-valued offset slipped in.** The anchor's offset reuses `AddDaysReferenceSchema`, whose `$field` string the `addDays` pair already admits dotted (#14104: "dot-path allowed exactly as $field allows it; SQL push-down applies the same same-table rule"). The anchor inherits exactly that declared asymmetry: validates, memory resolves it, SQL refuses by name — pinned on the corpus and on the analytics face — and no JOIN is planned anywhere. Letter A, not B-prime.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25808-now-anchored-comparand.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`; core, objectql, driver-sql, driver-mongodb, formula, service-analytics `patch`. The diff adds an authorable comparand shape to the published filter grammar (`data/NowAnchor:*` on the authorable surface, `NowAnchorSchema` on the api surface), so the kind is `added` and the level it owes is `minor` on the package that publishes the protocol — spec — which the changeset carries; the six executor packages publish no new authorable key or export of their own and take `patch`. Both declaration lines are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, plus `Ruling-ref: 6415710193`. No breaking marker, no ADR-0087 disposition owed (nothing removed or renamed). `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The `Clause-②:` line matches what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: yes (widening)

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's os-dev-report (6423037096) lists four deviations, two out-of-scope findings and an empty `open_questions`. Each answered:

1. **Files outside the claim surface** (core `filter-tokens.ts`, service-analytics `comparand-shape.ts` and the two strategies, spec `filter-comparand-type.ts` / `filter-lowering.ts`, driver-sql `index.ts` corpus export and seam test, sqlite-wasm conformance cell, the pin and strictness ledgers, regenerated artifacts) — **each necessary for the ruling**, judged above at ① items 3, 4, 6 and 11; the corpus export and the second sweep cell are what makes "pinned on both paths" true; the ledgers are gate-owned counters that move with the schema. Not a breach.
2. **No `engine.ts` edit** — answered at ① item 7: the judges `engine.ts` calls are the ones that grew.
3. **MySQL cell not executed locally** — accepted: the MySQL emission is pinned by the SQL-text cell on the PR; the live MySQL cell is `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` on main's full battery, which does not run on a PR (skipped on this head, as expected). Read by the publish lane, not this review.
4. **Commit trailer** in the repo's model-free form — compliant, no action.
5. **Prose overstatement, non-blocking, for the lane seat:** the PR body and changeset say the anchor is refused "by name" as a `$between` endpoint. It is refused (the endpoint union admits no object) but by zod's generic union text, not the anchor's own sentence; the schema docblock's "refused in every list position" is the accurate claim. Also one comment in core `filter-tokens.ts` (`isUnresolvedNowAnchor`) says a `$now: 'now'` is "left to the comparand-type door's plain-object refusal"; the door in fact keeps a string `$now` as the resolved form, and a non-instant string is refused loudly by driver-sql, the having judge and mongodb, and fails closed in the memory evaluator. Behaviour is correct and pinned; the comment and the "by name" phrase are the only inaccuracies. A follow-up comment fix, not a blocker.
6. **Out-of-scope finding, driver-memory answers `[]` silently** for a `{ $field }` comparand and therefore for an anchor — pre-existing, measured by the dev on the merge base, off this card's surface. No card exists for it yet (no issue since 17:00Z names it). **Escalated to the lane seat to file** under the dev's dedupe string "driver-memory cross-field comparand silent empty", per Prime Directive 10. Not this PR's defect.
7. **Out-of-scope finding, the RLS write-check seam** compares an anchor against a non-temporal column as written because `matchesFilterCondition` has no declaration map there — a boundary of the pre-existing `{ $field }` seam, noted in the PR's acceptance notes with no behaviour claimed. Accepted as stated; the declared seams (where, having, driver-sql) refuse.
8. **Ordinary queue landing.** Not governed (0 of 35 paths hit the register), 2682 changed lines under 3000, no fork, draft and un-armed at review time. After this PASS and the lane seat's ACCEPT the owning seat readies and arms it.

Gate verdicts on the head (48 check-runs, all completed): every one of the eight required contexts is `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and all eight shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`; `Lint UI` is `skipped` (no ui scope on this diff, the expected-skips roster). Also green: `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates` (the spec artifact gates), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Docs`, the three claim guards and `filter`. Skipped by design: `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the dogfood shards, `Test UI` shards, the two opt-in harnesses. No red to attribute to base: the `Test UI` 7/16 and 12/16 reds that main carried until #26231 did not run on this head at all. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-pgsc75`
Reviewed-by: `session_01RyMY3prh9GRva1Tt37Di3i`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · domain:spec seat 2 · 2026-10-26T18:08Z · head `9594f3737bf2cf0f4e2dd815372fe13d85e724bd`

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #25808`. 35 files, +2587/−95. `check-governed-merges --pr 26261`: NOT governed, 2682 changed lines (under 3000). `mergeable_state` clean.
2. **Premise and ruling.** Maintainer ruling A (6415710193): `{ $now: true, addDays: integer | { $field } }`, addDays required. The premise check 6420234055 corrected three paths only; the dev re-measured them. Letter A is implemented, not B′.
3. **Gates (check-runs pinned to this head).** 48 runs: 41 success, 7 skipped, 0 failed. `check-expected-skips --pr 26261`: OK (exit 0).
4. **Contract review.** PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head, comment 6423604143 (face `schema`; hits `filter.zod.ts`, `filter-comparand-type.ts`, `filter-lowering.ts`, and the deviations it judged necessary: core `resolveFilterTokens`, the spec sibling doors, the analytics decline).
5. **Remainder at `TIER_DEFAULT` (seat-read).** driver-sql `applyNowAnchorComparison`: the offset column passes the same gates as the `addDays` pair (declared, numeric, same table, not the tenant column, no dotted path); the target column and offset column bind as identifiers (`??`), the instant and literal days bind as values (`?`), nothing from the filter is interpolated into SQL text. Each predicate is null-total, so `$not` is the exact complement. The objectql having/aggregation judges, the formula memory path, the mongodb refusal and the conformance corpus match the changeset's per-package lines.
6. **Prose checked against the diff (changeset).** The seven per-package bullets hold against their hunks. Spec `minor`, six executors `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` match the moved authorable-surface and api-surface shards.
7. **Non-blocking, recorded here.** (a) The PR body says `$between` refuses the anchor "by name"; it refuses through its endpoint union with generic text. (b) The `isUnresolvedNowAnchor` docblock in `packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts` says a string `$now` falls to the door's plain-object refusal; the door keeps a string `$now` as the resolved form. Behaviour is right and pinned; only the comment is off.
8. **Out of scope.** The dev's finding (driver-memory answers `[]` silently for a `{ $field }` comparand, and so for the anchor) is the frozen gap of #15104 (closed not planned under #5499's driver-memory freeze). A pointer with this evidence goes on #15104; no new card.
9. **Landing.** Ready plus auto-merge.
